title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right anterior ankle at the malleoli under a linear probe, seen from the feet as on ultrasound: lateral on the image left, medial on the right, skin at the top.
teachingPoint: The deep peroneal nerve lies beside the anterior tibial artery, usually lateral to it, between the EHL and EDL tendons; the injectate surrounds the artery and nerve.
claims: Right ankle in section, seen from the feet: lateral on the left, the same way round as the positioning plate. Painted by Gemini from the code layout (commit d4915f7); probe, needle, injectate and labels drawn in code.
Anterior tibial artery with the deep peroneal nerve lateral to it (record, anatomy and steps).
Artery and nerve lie between the EHL tendon (medial) and the EDL tendons (lateral) (record, anatomy).
The artery, its veins and the nerve sit together in a thin fascial sheath on the tibia (painted; from the owner's NYSORA concept plate, which the record does not state).
Added standard anatomy: tibialis anterior tendon most medial, venae comitantes, extensor retinaculum, distal tibia.
Needle in-plane from lateral (owner, 2026-10-01: 'I want the needle coming in plane'), tip lateral to the nerve beside the artery.
Teal: injectate next to the artery, around the nerve (record, steps 5).
Four labels: Deep peroneal n., Anterior tibial a., EHL, EDL.

geometry.why: nerve lateral to the artery (lateral is left)
nerve beside, not in, the artery
bundle lies on, not in, the bone
needle enters lateral to the probe
needle stops short of the nerve
injectate lies on the tibia, not in it
